outcome: Rate of invasive procedures for hemorrhage control
cohort: 72,529 women delivering between 2011 and 2012 in 19 maternity units in two French perinatal networks
finding: The use of intrauterine balloon tamponade in routine clinical practice was associated with a significantly lower use of invasive procedures for hemorrhage control among women undergoing vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: The risk of an invasive procedure among women who delivered vaginally remained significantly lower in the pilot network (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0.14, 95% CI 0.08-0.27), but not for women who delivered by cesarean (adjusted OR 1.19, 95% CI 0.87-1.61).
